Turning fips mode on in a machine that isn't already configured for it will cause connection issues to anything not configured to work in fips mode. It is more likely that the user will lose access to their systems or important services than it working out of the box.
Automatically remediating this could cause some automated processes that require root access to fail. Since this will be site-specific this will not be enforced.

The product sets the maximum password age on every non-system user (UID 1000 and above with a login shell), including existing ones, but deliberately leaves the root account alone. This rule also requires root's maximum password age to be 60 days or less, even when its password is locked, so it fails on root alone.

The grub password is set via the password_pbkdf2 parameter, however, the rule explicitly checks for GRUB2_PASSWORD. The grub username and password are being set which meets the requirement of the rule, but the check for the rule is not checking for all possible methods of setting a password for a user.

The product applies nosuid to home directories only when they are NFS mounts, through simp_enterprise_el::mountpoints::nfs_mount_options. It does not change the mount options of a local /home, because remounting it could disrupt data access for logged-in users. On a local /home, or when /home is not a separate partition, this rule fails until the site adds nosuid to /home's fstab entry.

All system accounts found will be set to nologin except for the following: - root - sync - shutdown - halt The rule checks at least one of these accounts and flags it as a failure, which is a false negative. It is specifically failing because of the halt and sync accounts. Remediating these accounts could cause loss of access to the system or unexpected system failures.
The product cannot set a specific remote logging server. The user will need to configure this manually.

The product does not forward logs by default because the log server is site-specific. When a site enables forwarding (simp_rsyslog::forward_logs with simp_rsyslog::log_servers) and TLS logging (rsyslog::enable_tls_logging, with PKI), the forwarding actions in /etc/rsyslog.simp.d/10_simp_remote/ set StreamDriverAuthMode="x509/name" on the omfwd action. This rule only checks /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/ and accepts only the legacy $ActionSendStreamDriverAuthMode directive, so it cannot see them.

The product does not forward logs by default because the log server is site-specific. When a site enables forwarding (simp_rsyslog::forward_logs with simp_rsyslog::log_servers) and TLS logging (rsyslog::enable_tls_logging, with PKI), the forwarding actions in /etc/rsyslog.simp.d/10_simp_remote/ set StreamDriverMode="1" on the omfwd action. This rule only checks /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/ and accepts only the legacy $ActionSendStreamDriverMode directive, so it cannot see them.

The product does not forward logs by default because the log server is site-specific. When a site enables TLS logging (rsyslog::enable_tls_logging, with PKI), the product sets defaultNetstreamDriver="gtls" in the global section of /etc/rsyslog.simp.d/00_simp_pre_logging/global.conf, which the forwarding actions in /etc/rsyslog.simp.d/10_simp_remote/ use. This rule only checks /etc/rsyslog.conf and /etc/rsyslog.d/, so it cannot see that setting.

The rule wants $DefaultNetstreamDriver to be set to 'gtls', however, this is the legacy format for setting this parameter. The product will correctly set defaultNetstreamDriver to 'gtls' in the global section of /etc/rsyslog.simp.d/00_simp_pre_logging/global.conf, which will achieve the same thing.
